items.reason: Already closed in the tree: every ${{ }} in agent-dispatch.yml and autofix.yml sits in env:/if:/concurrency:, issue and comment text reaches scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs as AGENT_TASK_* env data, both jobs already declare minimal per-job scopes, and scripts/review/__tests__/gate-check.test.mjs pins those scopes plus a finding for interpolation inside a run: step — so editing anything here would be work for the scanner, not for the repo.

The blocking half landed (an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule on value imports of the @/app/_lib/db barrel, error, zero current violations, enforced by npm run lint in ci.yml node-quality and .githooks/pre-push), but the committed budget file this item asks for needs measured thresholds: the lane sandbox denies all execution, so I could neither run scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs nor calibrate perf-budget.json, and inventing ceilings would produce a gate that fails honest work or passes everything — a human runs `node scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs --record` and adds one `- run: npm run perf:budget` line to finish it.

Already closed in the tree: pipeline/jobfit/llm/fault.py (FaultProvider, 10 declared modes) plus pipeline/jobfit/eval/fault_eval.py run every fault against the real automation tasks with a recorded expectation each, gated at FAULT_THRESHOLD=1.0 through npm run test:eval:ci in ci.yml's python-gate — but the doc all four source files point at, docs/development/fault-injection.md, did not exist, which is plausibly why a scan reading the repo could not see the practice; I wrote it rather than touching the harness.

Needs a shell, a network and two installable versions: a rehearsed downgrade means building 0.2.0, running it against data/kp.sqlite, then starting 0.1.0 on the same file and recording what survived — this sandbox denies all execution, node_modules is absent, and no version after 0.1.0 exists yet, so anything I could write would be the documented procedure nobody has executed that the item explicitly rules out.

lessons: In this repository a scan gap is often already closed in code but invisible from the docs: the fault-injection drill was gated in CI while docs/development/fault-injection.md — referenced by four source files — was missing. Grep the referenced doc paths before assuming a practice is absent, and fix the dangling reference instead of rebuilding the practice.

The Ascent lane sandbox allows read-only shell (ls/grep/cat) but denies ALL execution, including `node <script>` and `node --check`. Any item whose artefact needs a measured baseline (a performance budget, a coverage threshold, a lockfile, a downgrade rehearsal) cannot be closed here — pick the sub-gap that is enforceable by a tool the repo already runs (an eslint selector rides `npm run lint`, which is in CI and the pre-push hook) and hand the measurement back as one named command.

kp's gate scripts follow a house shape worth matching: a long header stating the gap the gate closes, exported pure functions, --json, a ratchet that can only tighten unattended, a refusal to read an unparsable config as 'nothing to check', and colocated fixtures wired into ci.yml. A gate that flaps here gets deleted, so prefer a metric that is a pure function of the committed tree over a wall-clock one.
